_README: GENERATED-THEN-CURATED. Suites excluded from the full-suite shard job (scripts/run-vitest-shard.mjs) because they fail for reasons predating that job. Exists so the job can run EVERY other suite and be blocking now, rather than after all 1,283 suites are green. This list may only SHRINK: a path that no longer exists fails the runner rather than rotting here silently. Run just these with: node scripts/run-vitest-shard.mjs --quarantined. Seeded 2026-07-28 from a local census (335 suites, 39 failures), then extended from the first CI shakedown run (30351495703) which surfaced 109 failing suites across shards 4-8, plus 6 more from shard 3 once it stopped hanging (run 30353450584); with those, all eight shards were green. Notably most of the shard-1 failures are NOT the ones the local census found — they fail only on a Linux runner, which is why the census belongs in CI rather than on a Windows dev box. Dominant causes are stale queries and assertions left behind as the application changed underneath the tests: accumulated rot, not new breakage. Each entry is a suite to FIX and remove, not a permanent exemption. 2026-07-28 (second pass): 17 entries REMOVED after the quarantine visibility step showed them passing; each was then re-verified locally with --retry=0 so none was merely retry-rescued. 2026-07-28 (third pass): CreateCoursePage.test.tsx removed - fixed, 13/13. 2026-07-28 (fourth pass): Abbr.test.tsx and EnterpriseModules.test.tsx removed - both green (8/8 and 18/18). 2026-07-28 (fifth pass): 40 admin data-testid-cluster suites removed after retargeting their barrel mocks at the paths the pages actually import. GdprBreachDetail and UserShow stay: their testid failure is fixed but each has a second, i18n-dependent text assertion (no i18n resources load in tests), which belongs with the missing-text cluster. 2026-07-28 (sixth pass): RemainingModules.test.tsx removed - 12/12 after fixing an unstable useToast mock that caused an infinite render loop. 2026-07-29 (seventh pass): 8 entries REMOVED — the i18n-dependent-assertion cluster the sixth pass named as next. Each asserted the literal English a t() call produces, which no test can see because no i18n resources load in this environment; worse, the missing-key output is IDENTICAL for every value, so those assertions could not have distinguished view_profile from delete_data even in principle. Rewritten to assert a data-* attribute carrying the raw value the component received (UserShow status/role, GdprBreachDetail data categories, GdprBreaches severity, GdprAuditLog action, GdprConsents consent type, GdprRequests request type, ErrorLogs action, PermissionBrowser category). GdprConsents was doubly stale: its chip renders the API's human-readable consent_type_name and the fixture never set one, so the raw type was never on screen. All 8 verified together with --retry=0 (82/82), so none is retry-rescued. 2026-07-30 (eighth pass): GdprConsentTypes.test.tsx REMOVED — 12/12 with --retry=0, so not retry-rescued. Its recorded cause was wrong: this was never the AlertDialog slot="close" race, which by that reference only manifests in a real browser and not in jsdom. Both delete tests looked for the confirm button with textContent === 'confirm', but the page passes confirmLabel={t('enterprise.gdpr_delete')} and the setup loads the real English locale files, so the button reads "Delete". The lookup returned undefined and an `if (confirmBtn)` guard turned that into a silent no-click — the assertion failed having tested nothing. ConfirmModal's own tests passed throughout because they never override confirmLabel. Fixed by giving ConfirmModal's action buttons stable data-testid values (confirm-modal-confirm / confirm-modal-cancel) and targeting those instead of a label, which is the same i18n-independent approach as the seventh pass; one test also used waitFor(() => document.querySelector(...)), which resolves on a returned value and so never actually waited. STILL QUARANTINED and NOT this cluster: RoleForm (3, checkbox lookup by derived label), RoleList (1, error-message spy), LegalDocComplianceDashboard (1, a computed percentage, not a translation). 2026-08-05 (ninth pass): PerformanceDashboard.test.tsx REMOVED — 13/13 with --retry=0. One assertion expected "800ms" where Intl unit formatting emits "800 ms". Leaving it quarantined also cost a real bug: the page fetches /v2/metrics/summary, which is the event-counter endpoint and returns period/total_events/events_by_type, so summary.memory_spikes.length threw and the admin error boundary replaced the page — while all 12 tests passed against a mocked profiling payload no endpoint produces. There is no profiling backend at all (no table, no middleware), so the page now reports that the data is not collected instead of rendering zeroes. Three regression tests cover the real payload, a failed request, and a partial payload. 2026-08-27 (tenth pass): the last three enterprise-admin entries REMOVED — LegalDocComplianceDashboard, RoleForm and RoleList — leaving that module fully un-quarantined. All 35 tests across the three files verified with --retry=0, so none is retry-rescued. The three recorded causes were accurate and all three were stale-assertion rot of the kind this list exists to drain, except that one was a real product regression: (1) LegalDocComplianceDashboard expected '95.0%', written against a hand-rolled toFixed(1)+'%' that the page had already replaced with formatPercentValue() — Intl percent formatting emits '95%' for a whole number, so the assertion could not pass; a second test now pins the fractional case (95.42 → '95.4%') that actually exercises the formatter. (2) RoleForm's fixture invented permission slugs (reports.view, content.view) that AdminEnterpriseController::PERMISSIONS has never contained; the form resolves each slug to enterprise.permissions.<token> and falls back to 'Unknown permission', so no real label was ever on screen and the derived-label lookup recorded as the cause was a symptom. Retargeted at real slugs (content.blog.manage, users.view), which is what the page will actually be given. (3) RoleList was NOT a test fault: the page threw away the API's error message and always showed the generic enterprise.failed_to_delete_role, so an admin was never told WHY a delete was refused. Fixed in the component to `res.error || t(fallback)`, matching the 20 other admin call sites that already surface the server's own translated reason. 2026-08-27 (eleventh pass): the three FEED entries REMOVED — HashtagPage, HashtagsDiscoveryPage and PostDetailPage — leaving the feed module fully un-quarantined. All 31 tests across the three files verified with --retry=0, so none is retry-rescued. All three failed for ONE cause, and it was a test fault every time: the assertion asked for the WRONG ARIA ROLE, so it matched nothing and read as a missing control. (1) HashtagPage and PostDetailPage looked for role="button" on the back-to-feed control, which is `<Button as={Link}>` and therefore renders an `<a href>` with implicit role `link` — the correct element for something that navigates, so the pages are unchanged and the queries were fixed; both now also assert the href, because a named link that goes nowhere is the failure worth catching. HashtagPage had a second, compounding fault: its `Link` stub took only `{ children, to }` and discarded the rest, silently deleting the aria-label, so even a `link` query would have found an anonymous `<a>`; the stub now forwards its remaining props. (2) HashtagsDiscoveryPage asked for role="textbox", but SearchField renders `<input type="search">`, whose implicit role is `searchbox` — a textbox query can never match it. Two vacuous assertions found while in there were replaced rather than left: PostDetailPage asserted `document.body.textContent` was truthy (always true) and now checks the real "Item not found" message, and the search test re-asserted the element it had just found and now waits for the debounced request and the result it renders; a new test pins that a single character does NOT search.
